evidence: Supplier (batch 11): a Cartan subalgebra of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field is a Lie subalgebra that is nilpotent and satisfies N_g(h)=h, with no semisimplicity hypothesis. Consumer use: [L2] states this criterion and step 1.1 applies it to the lines R*K_0 and R*H to certify them as Cartan subalgebras of sl_2(R). Interface: sufficient - the supplier is the definition invoked, and both lines are one-dimensional abelian, hence nilpotent, with normalizer computed in the step.

Supplier (batch 11): sl_2(C) is the Lie algebra of traceless complex 2x2 matrices with basis e,f,h and relations [h,e]=2e, [h,f]=-2f, [e,f]=h. Consumer use: the Given and [L1] use the real algebra sl_2(R) with the matrices h,e,f,K_0=e-f and these bracket relations; steps 1.2 and 1.3 compute ad_{K_0} and ad_H in the basis (H,e+f,K_0). Interface: sufficient - the supplier fixes the matrices and all bracket relations, and the consumer takes their real span (the traceless real matrices), so no extra hypothesis is imported.

Supplier (batch 11): for a root alpha with Killing-dual H_alpha, the coroot h_alpha=2H_alpha/alpha(H_alpha) is well defined, satisfies alpha(h_alpha)=2 and B(h_alpha,H)=2alpha(H)/alpha(H_alpha). Consumer use: the Definition writes h_alpha=2H_alpha/alpha(H_alpha) as the coroot and uses alpha(h_alpha)=2 and the normalization [E,sigma E]=h_beta / [E,-theta E]=h_alpha. Interface: sufficient - the supplier defines exactly this element and its normalizing properties.

Supplier (batch 11): the Killing-dual vector H_alpha in h is the unique vector with B(H_alpha,H)=alpha(H) for all H in h; it is nonzero for alpha nonzero. Consumer use: the Definition writes "Let H_alpha in h be the Killing-dual vector of alpha" and uses the identity [X,Y]=B(X,Y)H_alpha for X in g_alpha, Y in g_{-alpha} to prove [E,sigma E]=h_beta and [E,-theta E]=h_alpha. Interface: sufficient - the supplier characterizes H_alpha exactly as used.

Supplier (batch 11): for a Cartan subalgebra h of a complex semisimple g, g_alpha={x:[H,x]=alpha(H)x for all H in h} and Phi(g,h) is the set of nonzero functionals with g_alpha nonzero; g=h+sum g_alpha with one-dimensional root spaces. Consumer use: the Definition fixes Phi=Phi(g,h) with root spaces g_alpha and uses theta(g_alpha)=g_{theta alpha}, one-dimensionality of imaginary root spaces, and the real/imaginary/complex classification. Interface: sufficient - the supplier fixes the root system and root spaces with the needed one-dimensionality.

Supplier (batch 11): a Cartan subalgebra of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra is a nilpotent subalgebra equal to its own normalizer; the definition is stated without a semisimplicity hypothesis. Consumer use: the Definition says g_0 is split if it contains a Cartan subalgebra h_0 ([[def-cartan-subalgebra-of-a-lie-algebra]]) whose adjoint operators are diagonalizable over R. Interface: sufficient - the supplier is the definition of the Cartan subalgebra required in the splitting condition.

Supplier (batch 11): a Cartan subalgebra of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra is a nilpotent subalgebra equal to its own normalizer. Consumer use: the Definition considers a Cartan subalgebra h_0 of a real semisimple Lie algebra ([[def-cartan-subalgebra-of-a-lie-algebra]]) and studies its theta-stability and decomposition h_0=t_0+a_0. Interface: sufficient - the supplier is the definition of the object being decomposed.
